customer_question: Our product uses a 'GATT Base Profile.' Does it require SIG PTS testing? We are not sure whether it is a standard SIG profile or a proprietary profile.
question_variants: Do proprietary BLE profiles require PTS testing?
What determines whether a profile needs SIG certification testing?
We use a custom GATT profile with 128-bit UUIDs — do we need to test it?
actual_issue: Customer ATAGO Co. asked whether their 'GATT Base Profile' required SIG PTS testing. The answer depends on whether the profile uses SIG-assigned 16-bit UUIDs (standard SIG profile → PTS test required) or customer-assigned 128-bit UUIDs (proprietary profile → no PTS test required).
plain_english_explanation: SIG only requires PTS testing for profiles and services that are formally standardized by the Bluetooth SIG, which are identified by their 16-bit UUID. If the customer has defined their own custom profile using a 128-bit (vendor-specific) UUID, it is proprietary — SIG has no test specification for it, so no PTS test is required.
consultant_answer: Confirm with the customer whether their profile uses a SIG-assigned 16-bit UUID or a proprietary 128-bit UUID. If 16-bit UUID → PTS test required. If 128-bit UUID → no PTS test required, and the profile is excluded from the certification test scope.
decision_logic: The boundary between testable and non-testable profiles is the UUID type: 16-bit = SIG standard profile = PTS test required. 128-bit = proprietary profile = no SIG test. This is a hard rule with no exceptions.
final_recommendation: Ask customers to identify the UUID of any profile listed on their RFQ. 16-bit UUID → include in PTS test scope. 128-bit UUID → exclude from scope and note as proprietary.
risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly including a proprietary 128-bit profile in the PTS test scope wastes testing cost. Incorrectly excluding a 16-bit SIG profile means the product is not fully qualified and may fail SIG review.
